study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study
exposure: Bishop score of ≤6 and dilation ≤2 cm
Women with an unfavorable cervix (Bishop score of ≤6 and dilation ≤2 cm) undergoing induction
Starting cervical dilation (<1 cm vs. ≥1 cm)
Gestational age at induction (≥41 weeks vs. 37-40w6d)
cohort: 854 women with a singleton gestation, intact membranes, and an unfavorable cervix undergoing induction of labor at ≥37 weeks gestation
finding: Women undergoing labor induction at ≥41 weeks gestation with an unfavorable cervix have a significantly increased risk of cesarean delivery compared to those induced at 37-40w6d.
mod_finding: Women at or beyond 41 weeks gestation undergoing induction with an unfavorable cervix have a significantly increased risk of cesarean delivery compared to women induced between 37 and 40 weeks and 6 days.
